Extends the single-level hash map to support adaptive SPH by creating multiple data structures for different cell sizes, utilizing the self-similarity of the Morton code ordering.
A specialized rendering structure that implicitly marks cells containing fluid surfaces to avoid checking empty cells during ray casting.
Memory scales with the number of occupied cells, not the domain volume.
*   **Limitations:** Hash collisions require verification (simulation) or result in conservative surface detection (rendering).
Morton code generation can be computationally expensive.
*   **When to Use:** Highly adaptive SPH simulations, real-time fluid rendering, scenarios with large empty spaces.

*   **When Not to Use:** Uniform density simulations where dense grids are more cache-friendly, or when exact surface reconstruction without potential false positives is critical without additional checks.
It was developed to address the limitations of dense data structures in Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations, particularly for adaptive resolutions and real-time rendering.
The method builds on earlier work by Green [Gre10] and Teschner et al. [THM*03], combining Morton codes with hash maps to achieve efficient spatial indexing.
